samples.xml_description:
<module id="parallel2serial">
    <description>Parallel to serial converter. Every 4 bits of parallel data are converted to 1 bit of serial data. Output valid_out indicates availability of serial output. When valid_out = 1, dout represents the most significant bit of d. In the next 3 cycles, the remaining bits of d are output sequentially.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="d" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit parallel data input.</input>
        <output id="valid_out">Valid signal indicating the availability of serial output.</output>
        <output id="dout">Serial output representing the converted data.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>Sequential logic block triggered on the rising edge of the clock or active low reset signal. If the reset signal is asserted, the counter register cnt is incremented by 1. Otherwise, if the counter value is 3, indicating the last bit of the parallel input, the module updates the data register with the parallel input, resets the counter to 0, and sets the valid signal to 1. Otherwise, it increments the counter by 1, clears the valid signal, and shifts the data register one bit to the left, with the most significant bit shifted to the least significant bit.</implementation>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width_description="[2:0]">Counter register initialized to 0.</reg>
        <reg id="valid">Valid signal initialized to 0.</reg>
        <reg id="data" width_description="[3:0]">Data register initialized to 0.</reg>
        
        <always @("posedge clk or negedge rst_n") begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 3'd0;
            end else begin
                if (cnt == 3'd3) begin
                    data <= d;
                    cnt <= 3'd0;
                    valid <= 1'b1;
                end else begin
                    cnt <= cnt + 3'd1;
                    valid <= 1'b0;
                    data <= {data[2:0], data[3]};
                end
            end
        end
        
        <assign dout = data[3];
        <assign valid_out = valid;
    </logic_description>
</module>
